cards.title: What is reported speech?
cards.body: Reported speech (also called indirect speech) is how we tell someone what another person said — without quoting their exact words.
cards.body_cz: Nepřímá řeč = říkáme, co někdo řekl, ale ne citujeme doslova v uvozovkách.
points: Direct: She said, “I am tired.” (exact words)
Reported: She said (that) she was tired. (we report the meaning later)

cards.title: When do we use it?
cards.body: When we pass on a message, retell a conversation, or summarise news — usually after a reporting verb in the past (said, told, asked).
cards.body_cz: Když předáváme zprávu, převyprávíme rozhovor nebo shrneme, co někdo řekl — často po said / told / asked v minulém čase.
points: He told me he would call later.
They said they had finished the work.
She asked if I was free.

cards.title: The basic pattern
cards.body: Reporting verb + (that) + clause. The verb in the clause often moves one step back into the past — that move is called backshift.
cards.body_cz: Oznamovací sloveso + (that) + vedlejší věta. Sloveso uvnitř se často posune o krok do minulosti — tomu se říká backshift (časový posun).
points: She said (that) she worked in Brno.
He told me (that) he would call.
that is optional in speech: He said he was tired.

cards.title: Backshift table
cards.body: If the reporting verb is past (said / told / asked), shift the tense in the reported clause like this:
cards.body_cz: Když je oznamovací sloveso v minulosti (said / told / asked), posuň čas ve vedlejší větě takto:

rows: They said they worked in Brno.
She said she would call me.

cards.title: say vs tell
cards.body: tell needs a person. say does not take a person object.
cards.body_cz: tell potřebuje osobu (komu). say osobu jako předmět nemá.
points: He told me he was tired. ✓
He said (that) he was tired. ✓
He said me he was tired. ✗ → He told me…

cards.title: Questions in reported speech
cards.body: Use asked + if/whether (yes–no) or asked + wh-word. Inside: statement word order — no do/does/did inversion.
cards.body_cz: asked + if/whether (ano/ne) nebo asked + wh. Uvnitř: oznamovací pořadí — bez do/does/did inverze.
points: “Are you free?” → He asked if I was free.
“Where do you live?” → She asked where I lived.
Not: She asked where do I live. ✗

cards.title: What does not always shift
cards.body: might, could, would, should, and ought to often stay the same. If something is still true now, speakers sometimes keep present — but this unit practises the standard backshift after past said/told.
cards.body_cz: might, could, would, should často zůstávají. Když je něco pořád pravda, někdy zůstane přítomný čas — tady trénujeme standardní posun po said/told v minulosti.
points: “I might be late.” → She said she might be late.
“I could help.” → He said he could help.

cards.title: Czech trap
cards.body: Czech often keeps one past or present look. English usually steps the verb back after said/told in the past.
cards.body_cz: Čeština často drží jeden čas. Angličtina po said/told v minulosti typicky posune sloveso o krok zpět.
points: Řekl, že je unavený. → He said he was tired. (not is, after said)
Řekla, že zavolá. → She said she would call. (will → would)

cards.title: What you practise
cards.body: Gaps hit the shifted form in the reported clause (was, worked, would, had, could…) and sometimes said/told.
cards.body_cz: Doplňuješ posunutý tvar ve vedlejší větě (was, worked, would, had, could…) a někdy said/told.
points: Read the whole line: who said what, and which tense fits after said/told.
Prefer tell + person; say without a person object.
